newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: COMMERCIAL BANK'S JAN-APRIL PROFIT UP.
newsitem.headline: COMMERCIAL BANK'S JAN-APRIL PROFIT UP.

text.p: Lithuania's State Commercial Bank said on Wednesday that its net profit in the first four months of 1997 was 5.6 million litas compared to 900,000 litas in the same period last year.
Audrone Vaitkiene, the director of the bank's economy department, also told Reuters that the bulk of its 1997 earnings came in April, when it posted a net profit of 5.3 litas.
The bank reported earlier its net profit in the first quarter was 347,000 litas.
"It was preliminary data and it was revised to 281,000 litas," Vaitkiene said
The state-run bank reported a staggering 172.8 million litas in losses in 1996 which stemmed from bad loans issued in 1992-1995.
The government last summer bailed the bank out of a serious liquidity crisis with a fresh injection of 165 million litas in share capital.
Vaitkiene also said that the bank's assets rose 319 million litas to 1.049 billion litas in the first four months of the year.
She also said that deposits at the end of April were 880 million litas versus 545 million litas at the beginning of 1997.
The loan portfolio of the bank declined at the end of April to 589 million litas from 607 million litas at the beginning of the year, Vaitkiene said.
The State Commercial bank is one of two state-run banks which have been slated for privatisation.
